item: Suspend freezer failure with a hard-NFS buffered reader, reproduced in an isolated VM

environment.nfs: nfs-kernel-server/nfs-common 1:2.9.1-1ubuntu1; client mount vers=4.1,hard,proto=tcp,nconnect=8,timeo=600,retrans=2 (the ROG options; one mount, not four)
environment.topology: NFS server in a network namespace behind a veth pair (not Wi-Fi), server-side 200 Mbit/s token-bucket shaper so the read is in flight; reader is dd with buffered 1 MiB reads of a 1.5 GiB file
environment.freezer: pm_test=freezer, state=freeze (s2idle), pm_freeze_timeout 20000 ms (the default, as on the ROG), pm_debug_messages=1 so the refusing task is printed
environment.transport_removal: ip addr flush + ip link set down on the client side; this approximates NetworkManager deactivation, NetworkManager itself does not run in the guest

link-up.reader: D in folio_wait_bit_common <- filemap_update_page <- filemap_get_pages <- filemap_read <- generic_file_read_iter <- nfs_file_read
link-up.outstanding_rpc: 2 READ tasks queued on the transport (xprt_pending)

link-down.outstanding_rpc: 2 READ tasks queued on the transport (xprt_pending)
link-down.freeze: failed after 20.007 s, 1 task refusing to freeze
link-down.refusing_task: dd (the reader), state D, trace io_schedule <- folio_wait_bit_common <- filemap_update_page <- filemap_read <- nfs_file_read

earlier_runs: Earlier iterations (5 s timeout, no nconnect, link down without address flush) gave the same outcome: link up froze in 0.006-0.010 s, link down failed. Two first runs hit the server grace period with the reader in an OPEN RPC wait (rpc_wait_bit_killable); those froze even with the link down. Their logs were not retained; they are context, not evidence.

networkmanager_1_58_1.finding: do_sleep_wake takes every managed hardware device down on suspend, skipping software devices and devices for which device_is_wake_on_lan() is true. That reads the live driver state (ethtool WoL, or Wi-Fi WoWLAN not NONE/IGNORE), not the NM setting. Skipped devices are unmanaged on wake to re-check connectivity; the code comment calls this taking them down post-suspend.

rog_context.mounts: four NFS 4.1 hard mounts from the media server, nconnect=8, timeo=600

comparison_to_rog: Same refusing-task stack from folio_wait_bit_common through nfs_file_read and the same -EBUSY outcome. Not shown identical: the ROG used Wi-Fi, four mounts, and NetworkManager itself; its exact folio, held locks and RPC state were not captured.
